title: Jared Kushner's hacked phone
summary: One specific allegation exists, but it rests on a single source. Matthew Cole's book 'Princes and Thieves', excerpted by Vanity Fair on 22 Oct 2026, says Russia's GRU hacked Kushner's personal iPhone in 2017-18 and that Dutch military intelligence (MIVD) gained screen-image access via a turned GRU hacker, seeing him log into a roughly $750M UAE/Saudi-funded account at First Abu Dhabi Bank. No government has confirmed it: the MIVD declined comment, and Kushner, his lawyer and Trump deny it. The firmly documented incident is narrower: in Oct 2024 Chinese Salt Typhoon hackers targeted Kushner's phone and call data via US telecoms, with no public evidence that his data was taken.

sub_claims.statement: A credible outlet has reported that Kushner's phone was hacked.
sub_claims.finding: Vanity Fair published an excerpt of national-security reporter Matthew Cole's book 'Princes and Thieves' (Simon & Schuster/Atria) on 22 Oct 2026. It was widely picked up by Dutch (NL Times, DutchNews, NOS) and US outlets. This confirms only that the allegation was reported, not that the hack happened.

sub_claims.statement: Russia's GRU compromised Kushner's personal iPhone in 2017-18, and Dutch MIVD obtained access by turning a GRU hacker.
sub_claims.finding: This is a single-source book claim resting on an unnamed source who called Cole in spring 2020; Cole does not say he saw the Dutch material. In the book's account the MIVD turned a GRU hacker in late 2017 (work for them or face arrest in Britain), gained access to GRU-held screenshots, and from early 2018 could see the screen while the phone was in use. There was no microphone, camera or manipulation capability. It is unclear whether Kushner knew. No US or Dutch official has confirmed any part of this.

sub_claims.statement: The screenshots showed Kushner accessing a roughly $750M Saudi/UAE-funded account (part of $1.75B-$2B in secret funds).
sub_claims.finding: The book alleges about $750M of Saudi and Emirati origin was routed via an Azerbaijani bank into a First Abu Dhabi Bank account held by the UAE government-funded Watani Al Emarat Foundation, with Kushner a signatory, not the owner. It also alleges about $1B sent via Azerbaijan to an Israeli government account and a third, defence-related account. Headline totals vary ($700M+, $1.75B, $2B). No bank records were published. Axios's Barak Ravid said parts 'don't add up', and the Jerusalem Post pulled its write-up, citing 'significant factual questions'.

sub_claims.statement: Official responses: denials from Kushner, his lawyer and Trump; no Dutch confirmation.
sub_claims.finding: The MIVD and the Dutch Defence Ministry told NOS and Reformatorisch Dagblad they do not comment on methods, knowledge or sources. Kushner called the claims 'completely insane' and said they 'never happened'. Chad Mizelle sent Condé Nast a letter on 23 Oct 2026 calling the excerpt defamatory per se and demanding takedown; it says Cole and Simon & Schuster were warned on 30 Jul and 10 Aug. Trump called it 'a totally false story' on 23 Oct, and White House communications director Steven Cheung called it 'baseless smears' and the book fiction. Simon & Schuster reportedly released the book a couple of days early (around 25-27 Oct) despite the legal threat. No suit, retraction or correction had been found by mid-Nov 2026.

sub_claims.statement: Congress has linked the alleged hack to his current envoy role in the Russia and Iran talks.
sub_claims.finding: Rep. Jamie Raskin (House Judiciary ranking member) demanded in Oct 2026 that Kushner recuse 'from negotiating or representing the United States in any capacity' in the Russia and Iran talks until he produces records of foreign-government payments, citing the slush-fund and GRU phone-hack reports. This extends Raskin's 17 Apr 2026 probe. That the GRU holds actual leverage over Kushner is inference, not reported fact. Raskin's letter says Kushner cannot serve as a US diplomat 'when at least five foreign governments — the Saudis, the Emiratis, the Israelis, the Russians, and even the Dutch — appear to have damning kompromat on you'; this is a political characterization of unverified allegations.

sub_claims.statement: Chinese state hackers (Salt Typhoon) targeted Kushner's phone and communications in 2024.
sub_claims.finding: In late Oct 2024 the NYT and others reported that China-linked hackers inside US telecom carriers targeted Eric Trump and Kushner, among others. The FBI said call logs and unencrypted texts may have been exposed. What was taken from Kushner was never disclosed. A source close to him said there was 'no indication that anyone got access to the data'. This is confirmed targeting; compromise is unproven.

sub_claims.statement: First-term communications-security concerns (WhatsApp with foreign leaders, Saudi spyware risk).
sub_claims.finding: In Mar 2019 Rep. Cummings said Kushner's lawyer Abbe Lowell had told the committee Kushner used WhatsApp for official business; Lowell disputed parts of that. A Saudi royal-court source told CNN that Kushner messaged MBS on WhatsApp (single source). WhatsApp patched an NSO spyware flaw in May 2019. In Jan 2020 UN rapporteur Agnes Callamard urged Kushner to check or replace his phone after the Bezos hack linked to an MBS account. None of this showed an actual compromise of his phone.

sub_claims.statement: Kushner's phone was compromised by Pegasus, Paragon or Iranian hackers.
sub_claims.finding: No credible report was found. Iran-linked groups leaked material from other Trump-circle accounts (e.g. Kash Patel's Gmail, Mar 2026). The Feb 2026 Gabbard whistleblower complaint concerns an NSA intercept of foreign nationals discussing Kushner, not a hack of his device.

sub_claims.statement: Social-media claims that Dutch intelligence 'confirmed' the hack or that Kushner is a foreign intelligence operative.
sub_claims.finding: Dutch authorities declined comment and confirmed nothing. Nothing in the book or in any verified record calls Kushner an operative; that version is viral distortion.

corrections: Headlines saying 'Dutch spies hacked Kushner's phone' compress the book's account: it says the GRU hacked the phone and the MIVD obtained screen images second-hand via a turned GRU officer.
The alleged monitoring dates to 2017-18 (Trump's first term), not his 2025-26 envoy period; its relevance to current talks is critics' inference.
Dollar figures in coverage are inconsistent ($700M+, $1.75B, $2B); the core alleged account is about $750M at First Abu Dhabi Bank.
The 2024 Salt Typhoon reporting shows Kushner was targeted, not that his data was stolen.
denials_and_context: Kushner: the claims are 'completely insane', 'outrageous and categorically false' and 'never happened'; he points to the absence of bank statements, account numbers or dates.
Chad Mizelle: 'no credible evidence'; 'There are no accounts and never were'; demand letter to Condé Nast on 23 Oct 2026 threatening defamation action.
Trump (23 Oct 2026): 'a totally false story', 'fake news'.
MIVD and the Dutch Defence Ministry: no comment on operational methods, sources or knowledge; neither confirmation nor denial.
Skeptics: Axios's Barak Ravid says key details 'don't add up' (e.g. a Bank of Israel account with Netanyahu as signatory); the Jerusalem Post removed its story over 'significant factual questions'.
Kushner's public denials centre on the accounts; no coverage found has him specifically addressing whether his phone was compromised.
Cole stands by the reporting (Democracy Now, 2 Nov 2026). Vanity Fair had not responded publicly to the takedown demand.
White House communications director Steven Cheung dismissed the article as 'baseless smears' and the book as fiction (late Oct 2026).
Audit re-check (mid-Nov 2026): no defamation suit filed, no Vanity Fair/Simon & Schuster retraction or correction, and no US or Dutch official confirmation found; Mizelle's post ended 'More to come.'
